- API spec summary (inline): Zotero Web API v3, base https://api.zotero.org/users/<id>, Zotero-API-Key header. Endpoint families: items (list/top/trash/get/children/fulltext, q+qmode=everything search, tag/itemType filters, since=version), collections (tree, items), tags, saved searches, fulltext index (?since cursor), deleted tombstones, /keys/current introspection. Sync = single monotone library version integer + Last-Modified-Version headers. Local SQLite cache with FTS5 over title/abstract/creators/tags/fulltext. The operator: sport-science director whose ritual is "search MY library before the open web" (research grounding), collection browsing, recently-added triage, bibtex export.

Inline absorb manifest (ALREADY covered — do not re-propose):
| # | Feature | Best Source | Our Implementation |
|---|---------|-----------|-------------------|
| 1 | API key auth + userID discovery | pyzotero | auth set-token + /keys/current doctor probe |
| 2 | Items list/search (q, qmode=everything, tag/itemType filters, || OR, - negation) | pyzotero | (generated endpoint) items list/top/trash |
| 3 | Item by key + children + citation includes | pyzotero | (generated endpoint) items get / items children |
| 4 | Collections tree + collection items | pyzotero | (generated endpoint) collections list/top/get/subcollections/items |
| 5 | Tags | pyzotero | (generated endpoint) tags list |
| 6 | Saved searches | pyzotero | (generated endpoint) searches list/get |
| 7 | Fulltext content + changed-index | pyzotero | (generated endpoint) items fulltext / fulltext changed |
| 8 | Deletion tombstones | pyzotero | (generated endpoint) deleted list |
| 9 | Incremental version-based sync into SQLite | prior CLI v0.1 (unique — no other tool) | framework sync + version cursors |
| 10 | Export formats (bibtex, ris, csljson) via format= | zotero-cli tools | (generated endpoint) items list --format bibtex |

## Pass 1 — Customer model (## Customer model): 2-4 concrete personas from the brief (the sport-science director + agent consumers at minimum), each with Today/Weekly ritual/Frustration. If the brief can't ground personas, return ONLY the '## Failure: brief lacks user research' envelope.

## Pass 2 — Candidates (## Candidates (pre-cut)): 8-16, labeled (a) persona-driven, (b) service content patterns (collections/tags/citekeys/fulltext), (c) cross-entity local queries over the SQLite cache, (e) user briefing (restore v0.1 surface + the brief's identified gap: v0.1 synced but had NO query path — offline FTS search is the headline), (f) codebase intelligence (Backoff/Retry-After honoring, version headers, Better BibTeX citekey backfill via local JSON-RPC 23119 with graceful degradation). Apply kill/keep checks inline. Long Description scope-redirects where command intents overlap.

## Pass 3 — Adversarial cut (## Survivors and kills): force-answer weekly-use / wrapper-vs-leverage / transcendence proof / sibling kill / buildability (spec-emits|hand-code) / long-description validity for each survivor. 4-8 survivors >= 5/10.
### Survivors table: | # | Feature | Command | Score | Buildability | How It Works | Evidence | Long Description |
### Killed candidates table: feature, kill reason, closest-surviving-sibling.

Output contract: exactly ## Customer model, ## Candidates (pre-cut), ## Survivors and kills. No other sections, no summaries. Your final message IS the document.

4	
5	## API Identity
6	
7	**Domain.** Zotero Web API v3 — the official read/write HTTP API for zotero.org-hosted research libraries. Base URL `https://api.zotero.org`, HTTPS only. Library-scoped URLs begin `/users/<userID>` or `/groups/<groupID>` (the `<userOrGroupPrefix>`). Versioning is pinned per-request via `Zotero-API-Version: 3` header or `?v=3` query param. A parallel **local API** (`http://localhost:23119/api/`, desktop app running) exposes the same read endpoints without auth and without the 100-item page cap — a viable secondary data source but not required for v1.
8	
9	**Users / personas.**
10	- **Primary operator: a sport-science director/researcher** (the user) with a large personal Zotero library of sport-science literature. He runs a `sports-science-research-grounding` workflow whose first step is "search my own Zotero library before searching the open web" — the CLI is the substrate for that ritual. He wants answers grounded in *his* curated corpus, offline, in seconds.
11	- **Agent consumers**: Claude Code skills (`pp-zotero-research-library` SKILL.md drives this binary with `--agent` mode) that need pipeable JSON, non-interactive auth, and stable exit codes.
12	- **Secondary**: any researcher scripting against a personal or group library (`--library user` | `--library group:<id>`).
13	
14	**Data profile.** Bibliographic items (journal articles, books, theses, reports…) with rich metadata: `itemType`, `title`, `creators` (array of `{creatorType, firstName, lastName}` or `{name}`), `abstractNote`, `DOI`, `date`, `publicationTitle`, `tags` (array of `{tag, type}`), `collections` (array of collection keys), `dateAdded`/`dateModified`, plus per-object integer `version`. Hierarchy: top-level items → child attachments/notes (`/items/<key>/children`). Collections are hierarchical (parentCollection). Full-text of indexed attachments is retrievable as plain text JSON. Everything is monotonically versioned by a single per-library integer — the foundation of cheap incremental sync.
15	
16	## Reachability Risk
17	
18	**None/Low.** Official, public, documented, stable API operated by the Zotero project (Corporation for Digital Scholarship). No scraping, no reverse engineering, no ToS gray areas. Auth is a user-created API key from <https://www.zotero.org/settings/keys>. Rate limiting is documented and cooperative (`Backoff` / `Retry-After` headers, ≤4 concurrent requests recommended). The API surface has been at v3 for a decade; the docs explicitly note v3 is current. Only soft risk: heavy full-library fulltext pulls on very large libraries should honor backoff to avoid temporary throttling.
19	
20	## Top Workflows
21	
22	1. **Incremental library sync** (the heartbeat): `sync` pulls items + collections (+ tags, deletions, fulltext) changed since the stored library version into a local SQLite cache. `GET <prefix>/items?since=<v>&format=versions&includeTrashed=1`, then batch-fetch changed items by key; `GET <prefix>/deleted?since=<v>` for tombstones. First run = full sync from version 0. This existed in the lost v0.1 and is the spine everything else hangs on.
23	2. **Research-grounding search** (the operator's key ritual): "what does my library say about hamstring injury prevention?" → local FTS over title/abstract/tags/fulltext in the SQLite cache, returning ranked items with citation-ready metadata (creators, year, DOI, abstract snippet). Answered **offline** from the cache; optional `--live` passthrough to `GET <prefix>/items?q=<terms>&qmode=everything`.
24	3. **Collection browsing/filtering**: list the collection tree, list items in a collection (`/collections/<key>/items[/top]`), scope searches to a collection. Mirrors how the operator organizes literature by topic/project.
25	4. **Tag-based retrieval**: list tags (`/tags`, `/items/tags` with filters), find items by tag (`?tag=<name>`; supports `||` OR-union and `-` negation search syntax), locally via the cache.
26	5. **Recently-added triage**: "what did I add this week?" — sort by `dateAdded desc` from the cache (or `?sort=dateAdded&direction=desc` live); pairs with export (`--format bibtex`) for dropping fresh citations into a manuscript.
27	
28	## Table Stakes
29	
30	Feature parity floor, derived from pyzotero (the dominant wrapper), the v3 API surface, and sibling CLIs (zotero-cli on PyPI/npm, pyzotero-cli, zotero-lib, the ~8 Zotero MCP servers on GitHub — all of which converge on search/collections/tags/fulltext/children as the core toolset):
31	
32	- **Items (read)**: list (`/items`, `/items/top`, `/items/trash`, `/publications/items`), get by key (`/items/<key>`, up to 50 keys via `?itemKey=k1,k2`), children (`/items/<key>/children`).
33	- **Collections**: `/collections`, `/collections/top`, `/collections/<key>`, `/collections/<key>/collections` (subcollections), `/collections/<key>/items[/top]`.
34	- **Tags**: `/tags`, `/items/<key>/tags`, `/items/tags` (filterable by `itemQ`/`itemTag`), per-collection tag endpoints.
35	- **Saved searches**: `/searches`, `/searches/<key>` (read + include in sync so deletions propagate).
36	- **Fulltext**: `/fulltext?since=<v>` (changed-content index) and `/items/<key>/fulltext` (content payload with `indexedChars/totalChars` or `indexedPages/totalPages`).
37	- **Search params**: `q` (phrase search of titles+creators), `qmode=titleCreatorYear|everything` (`everything` includes fulltext), `itemType`, `tag`, `since` — with `||` OR and leading `-` negation syntax.
38	- **Versions/sync**: `format=versions` (unpaginated key→version map), `?since=<version>`, `Last-Modified-Version` response header, `If-Modified-Since-Version` request header → `304 Not Modified`, `/deleted?since=<v>`.
39	- **Formats**: `format=json` (default; `include=data,bib,citation` with `style=<CSL style>`), `format=keys`, `format=versions`, and export formats usable as `format=`/`include=`: `bibtex`, `biblatex`, `csljson`, `ris`, `csv`, `mods`, `coins`, `tei`, `wikipedia`, etc. Export formats require explicit `limit` and don't support sorting/pagination when `format=bib`.
40	- **Key introspection**: `GET /keys/current` (and `GET /keys/<key>`) → `{userID, username, access:{user:{library,files,notes,write}, groups:{...}}}` — this is both the doctor probe and the **userID discovery path**: the operator only needs to paste an API key; the CLI resolves the numeric userID from `/keys/current` and verifies library access before saving config.
41	- **Prior-CLI carryover (user's stated vision: keep the same features)**: `auth login/status/logout`, `doctor`, `sync [--full|--dry-run|--no-bbt]`, `--library user|group:<id>`, `--agent` mode, env overrides (`ZOTERO_API_KEY`, `ZOTERO_USER_ID`, `ZOTERO_BASE_URL`), config at `~/.config/zotero-research-library-pp-cli/config.toml` (0600), exit codes 0/2/4/5/7/10, optional Better BibTeX citekey backfill via desktop JSON-RPC at `127.0.0.1:23119` (graceful degradation when app closed).
42	
43	## Data Layer
44	
45	Local SQLite cache (the prior CLI's design, now extended for search):
46	
47	- **Entities**: `items` (key PK, version, itemType, title, abstractNote, DOI, date/parsedDate, dateAdded, dateModified, creators JSON, raw data JSON, parentItem for children, deleted flag), `collections` (key, version, name, parentCollection), `item_collections` (join), `tags` + `item_tags` (join; tag type 0=manual/1=automatic), `searches` (key, version, conditions JSON), `fulltext` (itemKey, content, contentVersion), `sync_state` (library id, last library version per object type, last fulltext version, last sync timestamp).
48	- **Sync cursor** = the library version integer from `Last-Modified-Version`, stored per library (user vs each group) and per object class. Fulltext has its own version cursor via `/fulltext?since=`.
49	- **Deletions**: apply `/deleted?since=<v>` tombstones (collections, searches, items, tags) each sync.
50	- **FTS**: SQLite FTS5 virtual table over `title`, `abstractNote`, creator names, tag names, and `fulltext.content`, with rank + snippet() for research-grounding queries. Rebuildable from base tables (`sync --full` or a `reindex` maintenance path).
51	- **Multi-library**: keyed by library prefix so `--library group:1234567` gets its own cursor and rows.
52	
53	## Codebase Intelligence
54	
55	Exact wire-level facts for the spec (all verified against official docs):
56	
57	- **Auth header**: `Zotero-API-Key: <key>` (preferred) or `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; `?key=` query param exists but is discouraged. No auth needed for public libraries; local API reads are unauthenticated.
58	- **API version pin**: `Zotero-API-Version: 3` header (or `?v=3`).
59	- **Version headers**: response `Last-Modified-Version: <int>` on multi-object and single-object reads; request `If-Modified-Since-Version: <int>` → `304 Not Modified` when unchanged (multi-object today; single-object "in the future" per docs — treat single-object 304 as optional).
60	- **Pagination**: `start` (0-based) + `limit` (1–100, default 25 — **100-item hard page cap**); `Total-Results` response header gives full match count; `Link` response header carries `rel="next"/"prev"/"first"/"last"/"alternate"` URLs — follow `next` rather than computing offsets. `format=keys` and `format=versions` are exempt from the cap (return everything).
61	- **Rate limiting**: two mechanisms. (1) `Backoff: <seconds>` response header on otherwise-successful responses — server asks the client to pause that long before any further request; (2) `429 Too Many Requests` with optional `Retry-After: <seconds>` (also on `503` during maintenance) — wait at least that long, else exponential backoff. Keep concurrency ≤4. **pyzotero's known pain point (issue #98): it historically honored 429 but not the header-based `Backoff` — our CLI should honor both**, surfacing exit code 7 only after retries are exhausted.
62	- **Sync recipe** (docs' canonical order): `GET /keys/current` (verify access) → `GET /users/<id>/groups?format=versions` (group membership/versions) → per library: `collections?since&format=versions`, `searches?since&format=versions`, `items?since&format=versions&includeTrashed=1` → batch-fetch changed objects (≤50 item keys per `?itemKey=` request; collections up to 100 via `?collectionKey=`) → `GET /deleted?since=<v>` → store new `Last-Modified-Version`. If `Last-Modified-Version` changes mid-multi-page fetch, restart that phase (concurrent-modification guard).
63	- **Fulltext sync**: `GET <prefix>/fulltext?since=<v>` → `{itemKey: version}` map → `GET <prefix>/items/<key>/fulltext` per changed attachment.
64	- **Search syntax**: `tag=foo bar` (single), `tag=a||b` (OR), `tag=-foo` (NOT), same syntax for `itemType`; `q=` is phrase-only; `qmode=everything` adds fulltext to quick search.
65	- **Schema endpoint**: `https://api.zotero.org/schema` (whole schema, cacheable); `/itemTypes`, `/itemFields`, `/itemTypeFields?itemType=`, `/itemTypeCreatorTypes?itemType=` for piecemeal.
66	- **Landscape**: pyzotero (urschrei/pyzotero) is the reference implementation and now ships its own MCP server (`pyzotero-mcp`) with tools {search, get_item, get_children, list_collections, list_tags, get_fulltext} — a strong signal of the minimal agent-facing toolset. 67	
68	## User Vision
69	
70	Rebuild the lost CLI, same surface, same name (`zotero-research-library-pp-cli`), Go, Printing Press house style. Non-negotiables from the prior SKILL.md: `auth login` (prompt or flags; now enhanced — accept just the API key and auto-resolve userID via `GET /keys/current`), `auth status/logout`, `doctor` (config path, auth source, library target, live probe against `api.zotero.org`; exit 0 only when auth + connectivity pass), `sync` with `--full`, `--dry-run`, `--no-bbt`, incremental via the versions API into local SQLite; `--library user|group:<id>`; `--agent` (= `--json --compact --no-input --no-color --yes`); documented exit codes (0 ok, 2 usage, 4 auth, 5 API, 7 rate-limited, 10 config); env overrides; Better BibTeX citekey backfill when the desktop app is up.
71	
72	The operator's key ritual — the reason the CLI exists — is **research-grounding queries answered offline**: "what does my library say about X" must work with no network, sub-second, from the synced cache, returning citation-ready JSON his `sports-science-research-grounding` workflow can consume directly. v0.1 synced the data but shipped **no way to query it** (SKILL.md explicitly lists search/collections/tags/export as NOT implemented and tells agents to fall back to curl). Closing that gap is the whole point of the reprint.
73	
74	## Product Thesis
75	
76	**A local-first research-library engine, not an API wrapper.** Every existing tool (pyzotero, the CLIs, the MCP servers) is a thin live-API proxy: every question costs network round-trips, 100-item pages, and rate-limit exposure. This CLI inverts that: incremental version-based sync makes the SQLite cache a faithful replica (items, collections, tags, searches, fulltext, deletions), and FTS5 over title/abstract/creators/tags/fulltext makes "what does my library say about X" an offline, sub-second, agent-pipeable query. Live API access remains for freshness (`sync`) and passthrough (`--live`), but the default read path is local. For an agent-heavy user, this also means grounding workflows never burn rate limit or latency on repeated queries — sync once per session, query freely.
77	
78	## Build Priorities
79	
80	1. **P0 — Auth + doctor** (restore v0.1): `auth login/status/logout`, key validation + userID auto-discovery via `GET /keys/current`, config.toml 0600, env overrides, `doctor` connectivity probe, exit-code contract.
81	2. **P0 — Incremental sync** (restore + extend v0.1): full docs-recipe sync of items/collections/tags/searches + `/deleted` tombstones into SQLite; per-library version cursors; `--full`, `--dry-run`; mid-sync version-change restart guard; `Backoff`/`Retry-After`/429 handling with ≤4 concurrency.
82	3. **P0 — Search (the missing organ)**: `search "<query>"` over FTS5 (title/abstract/creators/tags), with `--tag`, `--type`, `--collection`, `--limit`, ranked output + snippets, `--agent` JSON with key/title/creators/year/DOI/abstract. This is the research-grounding command.
83	4. **P1 — Fulltext sync + search**: `/fulltext?since=` cursor + per-item content fetch into FTS; `search --fulltext` flag; when a fulltext hit is an attachment, resolve and return the parent bibliographic item (pyzotero-cli's proven pattern).
84	5. **P1 — Browse commands**: `collections list/tree`, `collections items <key>`, `tags list`, `items get <key>`, `items children <key>`, `items recent` (dateAdded desc) — all cache-first with `--live` passthrough.
85	6. **P2 — Export**: `export --format bibtex|csljson|ris` for a key list / collection / search result (live API `include=`/`format=` path; BBT citekeys from cache when present).
86	7. **P2 — Better BibTeX backfill** (restore): JSON-RPC to `127.0.0.1:23119`, `--no-bbt` skip, graceful degradation.
87	8. **Deferred**: writes (item create/edit/delete), attachments/PDF download, group-library multi-sync orchestration, OAuth flow (dedicated keys suffice for a single-operator tool).

2. **Research-grounding search** (the operator's key ritual): "what does my library say about hamstring injury prevention?" → local FTS over title/abstract/tags/fulltext in the SQLite cache, returning ranked items with citation-ready metadata (creators, year, DOI, abstract snippet). Answered **offline** from the cache; optional `--live` passthrough to `GET <prefix>/items?q=<terms>&qmode=everything`.
3. **Collection browsing/filtering**: list the collection tree, list items in a collection (`/collections/<key>/items[/top]`), scope searches to a collection. Mirrors how the operator organizes literature by topic/project.
4. **Tag-based retrieval**: list tags (`/tags`, `/items/tags` with filters), find items by tag (`?tag=<name>`; supports `||` OR-union and `-` negation search syntax), locally via the cache.
5. **Recently-added triage**: "what did I add this week?" — sort by `dateAdded desc` from the cache (or `?sort=dateAdded&direction=desc` live); pairs with export (`--format bibtex`) for dropping fresh citations into a manuscript.

## Table Stakes

Feature parity floor, derived from pyzotero (the dominant wrapper), the v3 API surface, and sibling CLIs (zotero-cli on PyPI/npm, pyzotero-cli, zotero-lib, the ~8 Zotero MCP servers on GitHub — all of which converge on search/collections/tags/fulltext/children as the core toolset):

- **Items (read)**: list (`/items`, `/items/top`, `/items/trash`, `/publications/items`), get by key (`/items/<key>`, up to 50 keys via `?itemKey=k1,k2`), children (`/items/<key>/children`).
- **Collections**: `/collections`, `/collections/top`, `/collections/<key>`, `/collections/<key>/collections` (subcollections), `/collections/<key>/items[/top]`.
- **Tags**: `/tags`, `/items/<key>/tags`, `/items/tags` (filterable by `itemQ`/`itemTag`), per-collection tag endpoints.
- **Saved searches**: `/searches`, `/searches/<key>` (read + include in sync so deletions propagate).
- **Fulltext**: `/fulltext?since=<v>` (changed-content index) and `/items/<key>/fulltext` (content payload with `indexedChars/totalChars` or `indexedPages/totalPages`).
- **Search params**: `q` (phrase search of titles+creators), `qmode=titleCreatorYear|everything` (`everything` includes fulltext), `itemType`, `tag`, `since` — with `||` OR and leading `-` negation syntax.
- **Versions/sync**: `format=versions` (unpaginated key→version map), `?since=<version>`, `Last-Modified-Version` response header, `If-Modified-Since-Version` request header → `304 Not Modified`, `/deleted?since=<v>`.
- **Formats**: `format=json` (default; `include=data,bib,citation` with `style=<CSL style>`), `format=keys`, `format=versions`, and export formats usable as `format=`/`include=`: `bibtex`, `biblatex`, `csljson`, `ris`, `csv`, `mods`, `coins`, `tei`, `wikipedia`, etc. Export formats require explicit `limit` and don't support sorting/pagination when `format=bib`.
- **Key introspection**: `GET /keys/current` (and `GET /keys/<key>`) → `{userID, username, access:{user:{library,files,notes,write}, groups:{...}}}` — this is both the doctor probe and the **userID discovery path**: the operator only needs to paste an API key; the CLI resolves the numeric userID from `/keys/current` and verifies library access before saving config.
- **Prior-CLI carryover (user's stated vision: keep the same features)**: `auth login/status/logout`, `doctor`, `sync [--full|--dry-run|--no-bbt]`, `--library user|group:<id>`, `--agent` mode, env overrides (`ZOTERO_API_KEY`, `ZOTERO_USER_ID`, `ZOTERO_BASE_URL`), config at `~/.config/zotero-research-library-pp-cli/config.toml` (0600), exit codes 0/2/4/5/7/10, optional Better BibTeX citekey backfill via desktop JSON-RPC at `127.0.0.1:23119` (graceful degradation when app closed).

## Data Layer

Local SQLite cache (the prior CLI's design, now extended for search):

- **Entities**: `items` (key PK, version, itemType, title, abstractNote, DOI, date/parsedDate, dateAdded, dateModified, creators JSON, raw data JSON, parentItem for children, deleted flag), `collections` (key, version, name, parentCollection), `item_collections` (join), `tags` + `item_tags` (join; tag type 0=manual/1=automatic), `searches` (key, version, conditions JSON), `fulltext` (itemKey, content, contentVersion), `sync_state` (library id, last library version per object type, last fulltext version, last sync timestamp).
- **Sync cursor** = the library version integer from `Last-Modified-Version`, stored per library (user vs each group) and per object class. Fulltext has its own version cursor via `/fulltext?since=`.
- **Deletions**: apply `/deleted?since=<v>` tombstones (collections, searches, items, tags) each sync.
- **FTS**: SQLite FTS5 virtual table over `title`, `abstractNote`, creator names, tag names, and `fulltext.content`, with rank + snippet() for research-grounding queries. Rebuildable from base tables (`sync --full` or a `reindex` maintenance path).
- **Multi-library**: keyed by library prefix so `--library group:1234567` gets its own cursor and rows.

## Codebase Intelligence

Exact wire-level facts for the spec (all verified against official docs):

- **Auth header**: `Zotero-API-Key: <key>` (preferred) or `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; `?key=` query param exists but is discouraged. No auth needed for public libraries; local API reads are unauthenticated.
- **API version pin**: `Zotero-API-Version: 3` header (or `?v=3`).
- **Version headers**: response `Last-Modified-Version: <int>` on multi-object and single-object reads; request `If-Modified-Since-Version: <int>` → `304 Not Modified` when unchanged (multi-object today; single-object "in the future" per docs — treat single-object 304 as optional).
- **Pagination**: `start` (0-based) + `limit` (1–100, default 25 — **100-item hard page cap**); `Total-Results` response header gives full match count; `Link` response header carries `rel="next"/"prev"/"first"/"last"/"alternate"` URLs — follow `next` rather than computing offsets. `format=keys` and `format=versions` are exempt from the cap (return everything).
- **Rate limiting**: two mechanisms. (1) `Backoff: <seconds>` response header on otherwise-successful responses — server asks the client to pause that long before any further request; (2) `429 Too Many Requests` with optional `Retry-After: <seconds>` (also on `503` during maintenance) — wait at least that long, else exponential backoff. Keep concurrency ≤4. **pyzotero's known pain point (issue #98): it historically honored 429 but not the header-based `Backoff` — our CLI should honor both**, surfacing exit code 7 only after retries are exhausted.
- **Sync recipe** (docs' canonical order): `GET /keys/current` (verify access) → `GET /users/<id>/groups?format=versions` (group membership/versions) → per library: `collections?since&format=versions`, `searches?since&format=versions`, `items?since&format=versions&includeTrashed=1` → batch-fetch changed objects (≤50 item keys per `?itemKey=` request; collections up to 100 via `?collectionKey=`) → `GET /deleted?since=<v>` → store new `Last-Modified-Version`. If `Last-Modified-Version` changes mid-multi-page fetch, restart that phase (concurrent-modification guard).
- **Fulltext sync**: `GET <prefix>/fulltext?since=<v>` → `{itemKey: version}` map → `GET <prefix>/items/<key>/fulltext` per changed attachment.
- **Search syntax**: `tag=foo bar` (single), `tag=a||b` (OR), `tag=-foo` (NOT), same syntax for `itemType`; `q=` is phrase-only; `qmode=everything` adds fulltext to quick search.
- **Schema endpoint**: `https://api.zotero.org/schema` (whole schema, cacheable); `/itemTypes`, `/itemFields`, `/itemTypeFields?itemType=`, `/itemTypeCreatorTypes?itemType=` for piecemeal.
- **Landscape**: pyzotero (urschrei/pyzotero) is the reference implementation and now ships its own MCP server (`pyzotero-mcp`) with tools {search, get_item, get_children, list_collections, list_tags, get_fulltext} — a strong signal of the minimal agent-facing toolset. CLI competitors: `zotero-cli`/`pyzotero-cli`/`zotero-cli-tool` (PyPI), `zotero-lib` (npm, OpenDevEd). ~8+ Zotero MCP servers exist on GitHub (54yyyu/zotero-mcp, kujenga/zotero-mcp, masaki39 local-API variant, etc.); none pair an offline SQLite FTS cache with incremental version-based sync — that combination is this CLI's differentiator.

## User Vision

Rebuild the lost CLI, same surface, same name (`zotero-research-library-pp-cli`), Go, Printing Press house style. Non-negotiables from the prior SKILL.md: `auth login` (prompt or flags; now enhanced — accept just the API key and auto-resolve userID via `GET /keys/current`), `auth status/logout`, `doctor` (config path, auth source, library target, live probe against `api.zotero.org`; exit 0 only when auth + connectivity pass), `sync` with `--full`, `--dry-run`, `--no-bbt`, incremental via the versions API into local SQLite; `--library user|group:<id>`; `--agent` (= `--json --compact --no-input --no-color --yes`); documented exit codes (0 ok, 2 usage, 4 auth, 5 API, 7 rate-limited, 10 config); env overrides; Better BibTeX citekey backfill when the desktop app is up.

The operator's key ritual — the reason the CLI exists — is **research-grounding queries answered offline**: "what does my library say about X" must work with no network, sub-second, from the synced cache, returning citation-ready JSON his `sports-science-research-grounding` workflow can consume directly. v0.1 synced the data but shipped **no way to query it** (SKILL.md explicitly lists search/collections/tags/export as NOT implemented and tells agents to fall back to curl). Closing that gap is the whole point of the reprint.

## Product Thesis

**A local-first research-library engine, not an API wrapper.** Every existing tool (pyzotero, the CLIs, the MCP servers) is a thin live-API proxy: every question costs network round-trips, 100-item pages, and rate-limit exposure. This CLI inverts that: incremental version-based sync makes the SQLite cache a faithful replica (items, collections, tags, searches, fulltext, deletions), and FTS5 over title/abstract/creators/tags/fulltext makes "what does my library say about X" an offline, sub-second, agent-pipeable query. Live API access remains for freshness (`sync`) and passthrough (`--live`), but the default read path is local. For an agent-heavy user, this also means grounding workflows never burn rate limit or latency on repeated queries — sync once per session, query freely.

## Build Priorities

1. **P0 — Auth + doctor** (restore v0.1): `auth login/status/logout`, key validation + userID auto-discovery via `GET /keys/current`, config.toml 0600, env overrides, `doctor` connectivity probe, exit-code contract.
2. **P0 — Incremental sync** (restore + extend v0.1): full docs-recipe sync of items/collections/tags/searches + `/deleted` tombstones into SQLite; per-library version cursors; `--full`, `--dry-run`; mid-sync version-change restart guard; `Backoff`/`Retry-After`/429 handling with ≤4 concurrency.
3. **P0 — Search (the missing organ)**: `search "<query>"` over FTS5 (title/abstract/creators/tags), with `--tag`, `--type`, `--collection`, `--limit`, ranked output + snippets, `--agent` JSON with key/title/creators/year/DOI/abstract. This is the research-grounding command.
4. **P1 — Fulltext sync + search**: `/fulltext?since=` cursor + per-item content fetch into FTS; `search --fulltext` flag; when a fulltext hit is an attachment, resolve and return the parent bibliographic item (pyzotero-cli's proven pattern).
5. **P1 — Browse commands**: `collections list/tree`, `collections items <key>`, `tags list`, `items get <key>`, `items children <key>`, `items recent` (dateAdded desc) — all cache-first with `--live` passthrough.
6. **P2 — Export**: `export --format bibtex|csljson|ris` for a key list / collection / search result (live API `include=`/`format=` path; BBT citekeys from cache when present).
7. **P2 — Better BibTeX backfill** (restore): JSON-RPC to `127.0.0.1:23119`, `--no-bbt` skip, graceful degradation.
8. **Deferred**: writes (item create/edit/delete), attachments/PDF download, group-library multi-sync orchestration, OAuth flow (dedicated keys suffice for a single-operator tool).

## Customer model

**P1 — The sport-science director (the operator).** Today: runs a `sports-science-research-grounding` workflow whose step 1 is "search MY Zotero library before the open web," but v0.1 synced data with zero query path, so the step falls back to curl or the desktop app. Weekly ritual: 5-15 grounding queries ("what does my library say about hamstring injury prevention?"), collection browsing by topic/project, Friday triage of what was added this week, dropping fresh citations into a manuscript as bibtex. Frustration: the answers exist in his curated corpus and in a synced SQLite file on disk, and he still can't ask them from a terminal — every question costs network, 100-item pages, and rate-limit exposure.

**P2 — The agent consumer (Claude Code skills).** Today: `pp-zotero-research-library` SKILL.md explicitly instructs agents to STOP and shell out to curl for anything beyond auth/doctor/sync. Weekly ritual: dozens of automated invocations per session inside grounding workflows — needs `--agent` JSON, stable exit codes (0/2/4/5/7/10), non-interactive auth, and zero-latency repeated queries that don't burn the rate limit. Frustration: repeated live-API round-trips inside agent loops trip `Backoff`/429 (pyzotero issue #98 shows even the reference wrapper got this wrong), and there's no offline read path to hit instead.

**P3 — The manuscript/export scripter (same human, writing hat; also any group-library member).** Today: exports citations via the Zotero desktop GUI or hand-rolled `format=bibtex` curl. Weekly ritual: turn a search result or a collection into a bibtex/CSL-JSON block with the *Better BibTeX citekeys his .tex files already use* — plain Web API export doesn't know BBT citekeys. Frustration: the Web API's export formats and the desktop's BBT citekeys live in two disconnected worlds; `--library group:<id>` scripting has the same gap.

## Candidates (pre-cut)

1. **(e) `search` — offline FTS5 research-grounding search** [HEADLINE]. Ranked FTS5 over title/abstract/creators/tags in the synced cache, with `snippet()`, `--tag`/`--type`/`--collection`/`--limit` filters, `--live` passthrough to `?q=&qmode=everything`, `--agent` JSON with key/title/creators/year/DOI/abstract. Kill/keep: mechanical, local data, no LLM. **Keep.** This is the brief's stated "whole point of the reprint."
2. **(e) `search --fulltext`** — extend FTS to `fulltext.content`; when a hit is an attachment, resolve and return the parent bibliographic item (pyzotero-cli's proven pattern). Kill/keep: local data; parent-resolution is one JOIN. Keep as a *flag on #1*, not a sibling command — merge candidate.
3. **(a) `grounding` one-shot answer pack** — query → top-k items + snippets + bibtex in one envelope shaped for the workflow skill. Kill/keep: identical data path to `search --agent`; sibling-overlap suspect from birth.
4. **(c) `items recent`** — `dateAdded DESC` triage from the cache with `--days N`/`--limit`, pipeable into export. Kill/keep: pure local ORDER BY. **Keep** (brief workflow #5).
5. **(b) `collections tree`** — render the full hierarchy (API returns flat parentCollection rows; the tree is a local recursion the API can't do in one call), with per-node item counts from the join table. Kill/keep: local, mechanical. **Keep.**
6. **(f) `Backoff`/`Retry-After` honoring in the transport** — honor both the header-based `Backoff: <s>` on 200s AND `429/503 Retry-After`, ≤4 concurrency, exit 7 only after retries exhausted; plus the `Last-Modified-Version` mid-fetch restart guard. pyzotero historically honored only 429 (issue #98) — no sibling tool gets this right. Kill/keep: not a command but a differentiating hand-code layer every live call inherits. **Keep, framed as sync/transport hardening.**
7. **(f) `cite <citekey>` + BBT citekey backfill** — restore v0.1's Better BibTeX JSON-RPC backfill (127.0.0.1:23119, graceful degradation, `--no-bbt`), then add the payoff v0.1 never had: look items up *by citekey* from the cache and export with citekeys attached. Kill/keep: external service is localhost/free/no-auth and already in the brief. **Keep.**
8. **(c) `cache status` / `cache reindex`** — last sync time, per-object version cursors, row/FTS counts, staleness warning; `reindex` rebuilds FTS5 from base tables without a network `--full` resync (brief's Data Layer explicitly calls the FTS "rebuildable"). Kill/keep: local, mechanical, doctor's offline sibling. **Keep.**
9. **(c) `related <key>`** — rank cache items by shared tags/collections with a given item. Kill/keep: buildable but no research evidence of demand; `search --tag` covers the honest version.
10. **(c) `dupes`** — detect duplicates by normalized DOI/title in the cache. Kill/keep: buildable, but zero evidence in the brief; triage is monthly at best.
11. **(b) local saved-search execution** — the Web API returns saved-search *definitions* but cannot execute them; translate the conditions JSON to local SQL. Kill/keep: genuine API gap, but conditions JSON has dozens of operator/field combos — >200-line application territory, and the brief provides no demand evidence. Buildability suspect.
12. **(c) `stats`** — item counts by type/year/top tags. Kill/keep: mechanical but speculative; overlaps `cache status` counts.
13. **(a) `watch` for new items** — kill/keep: persistent process = scope creep; poll-once IS `items recent`.
14. **(b) tag co-occurrence suggestions** — kill/keep: drifts toward semantic grouping (LLM-dependency check) and no evidence.
15. **(a) `export` of search-result/collection keys with citekeys** — the manifest's #10 covers live `format=bibtex` on list endpoints; the novel sliver is exporting an arbitrary key list enriched with cached BBT citekeys. Merge candidate into #7's citekey feature; Long Description scope-redirect against manifest #10.
16. **(c) cache-first read layer with global `--live`** — kill/keep: cross-cutting architecture (Build Priority P1), not a feature row; it ships inside #1/#4/#5 rather than as its own entry.

## Survivors and kills

Forced answers applied to each survivor — weekly use (P1 ritual or P2 loop frequency), wrapper-vs-leverage (does it do something the raw API cannot?), transcendence proof, sibling kill, buildability class, long-description validity (referenced commands all survive below).

| # | Feature | Command | Score | Buildability | How It Works | Evidence | Long Description |
|---|---------|---------|-------|--------------|--------------|----------|------------------|
| 1 | Offline research-grounding search (incl. `--fulltext` with parent-item resolution, `--live` passthrough) | `search "<query>" [--tag --type --collection --fulltext --live --limit]` | 10/10 | hand-code | Queries the SQLite FTS5 table over title/abstract/creators/tags/fulltext.content with rank + snippet(); fulltext attachment hits JOIN to parentItem; `--live` falls through to `GET /items?q=&qmode=everything` | Prior SKILL.md explicitly lists search as NOT implemented and tells agents to curl; brief calls closing this gap "the whole point of the reprint"; no sibling tool (pyzotero, 8+ MCP servers) pairs offline FTS with version sync | Use this for "what does my library say about X" — answers offline from the synced cache, sub-second. Do NOT use `items list --live` for text search unless you need unsynced server state; run `sync` first instead. |
| 2 | Backoff-correct transport + mid-sync version guard | (transport layer under `sync` and all `--live` calls) | 9/10 | hand-code | HTTP client honors `Backoff: <s>` on successful responses AND `Retry-After` on 429/503 with ≤4 concurrency and exponential fallback; restarts a fetch phase when `Last-Modified-Version` shifts mid-pagination; exit 7 only after retries exhausted | Official docs specify both mechanisms; pyzotero issue #98 documents the reference wrapper honoring only 429 — an explicit competitor gap named in the brief's Codebase Intelligence | none |
| 3 | Recently-added triage | `items recent [--days N --limit N]` | 8/10 | hand-code | `SELECT ... FROM items WHERE NOT deleted ORDER BY dateAdded DESC` on the local cache, with `--days` cutoff; pipeable keys feed `export` | Brief Top Workflow #5 ("what did I add this week?") and the operator's stated Friday triage + manuscript-citation pairing | Use for time-based triage of new additions. For topic queries use `search`; for full listings use the generated `items list`. |
| 4 | Citekey bridge: BBT backfill + citekey lookup/export | `cite <citekey> [--format bibtex]` + `sync` backfill (`--no-bbt`) | 7/10 | hand-code | `sync` calls Better BibTeX JSON-RPC at `127.0.0.1:23119` to store citekeys in the cache (graceful skip when desktop closed); `cite` resolves citekey→item locally and emits metadata or citekey-faithful bibtex | Prior CLI v0.1 shipped the backfill (user said keep it); brief P2 priority; Web API export cannot know BBT citekeys — a gap only a local bridge closes | Use `cite` to resolve a Better BibTeX citekey to its item or export it. For bulk export by collection or key list without citekeys, use the generated `items list --format bibtex`. |
| 5 | Cached collection tree with counts | `collections tree [--counts]` | 7/10 | hand-code | Recursively assembles parentCollection links from the local `collections` table and counts via `item_collections` join — a shape the flat API cannot return in one call | Brief Top Workflow #3 (collection browsing mirrors how the operator organizes literature); pyzotero requires N+1 calls (`all_collections` walk) for the same view | Use for the hierarchical overview. For raw per-collection membership or live state, use the generated `collections list` / `collections items`. |
| 6 | Cache health + offline reindex | `cache status` / `cache reindex` | 7/10 | hand-code | Reads `sync_state` cursors, row counts, FTS row counts, last-sync age from SQLite; `reindex` rebuilds the FTS5 virtual table from base tables with zero network | Brief Data Layer marks FTS "rebuildable (`sync --full` or a `reindex` maintenance path)"; prior SKILL.md's only corruption remedy was a full network resync | Use `cache status` for offline cache introspection; use `doctor` when you need the live connectivity probe. `cache reindex` never touches the network — prefer it over `sync --full` for local index corruption. |

Buildability proofs (rubric sentence): #1 uses the local FTS5 table (+ optional `GET /items?q=`) to compute ranked snippets with no external dependencies; #2 uses documented response headers to compute retry timing; #3/#5/#6 use local SQLite tables only; #4 uses the brief-documented localhost JSON-RPC with graceful degradation.

**Killed candidates**

| Feature | Kill reason | Closest surviving sibling |
|---|---|---|
| `grounding` answer pack | Identical data path to `search --agent`; a second command name for the same query invites agent tool-confusion | `search` (#1) |
| `search --fulltext` as separate command | Merged — one flag on the same FTS index, not a sibling command | `search` (#1) |
| Local saved-search execution | Buildability: conditions JSON is an open-ended operator/field matrix (>200-line application); zero demand evidence in Phase 1 research | `search` (#1) with `--tag/--type/--collection` |
| `related <key>` | Speculative (User Pain 1, Research Backing 0); tag-overlap ranking without evidence | `search --tag` (#1) |
| `dupes` | No evidence in brief or landscape; monthly-at-best use fails weekly-use test | `search` (#1) for manual DOI checks |
| `stats` library overview | Sibling overlap — counts already surface in `cache status`; standalone version is speculative | `cache status` (#6) |
| `watch` new-item monitor | Scope creep (persistent process); poll-once form already exists | `items recent` (#3) |
| Tag co-occurrence suggestions | Drifts into semantic grouping (LLM-dependency kill) and has no research backing | generated `tags list` |
| Search-result export with citekeys (standalone) | Merged into the citekey bridge; live-format export is absorb manifest #10 | `cite` (#4) / manifest #10 |
| Cache-first `--live` read layer | Cross-cutting architecture (Build Priority P1), not a feature row — ships inside #1/#3/#5 | `search` (#1) |
